text:
marta: FYI opened a small PR to fix the embeddings API reference. The request example still shows `input` as a string which makes it look like batch calls aren't supported. Links: PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4721 and rendered draft: https://deploy-preview.docs/4721

kevin: quick context: we standardized on `input` being an array for batch semantics a while ago. the runtime still accepts a single string for backwards compat, but docs should show arrays so users assume batching by default.

marta: exact wrong snippet on page is:
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "open-embed-1",
  "input": "single string"
}
```
which the linter flagged as wrong and confuses support. i propose changing to:
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "open-embed-1",
  "input": ["single string", "another sentence"]
}
```
and add a one-paragraph note: "Clients and server normalize single-item inputs; SDKs prefer/emit arrays for batch indexing workloads."

sam: also add the response example note. folks keep misinterpreting `data` as one item. servers return `data` as an array of objects matching the input order. example response snippet i added: 
```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {"object": "embedding", "embedding": [0.01, ...], "index": 0},
    {"object": "embedding", "embedding": [0.02, ...], "index": 1}
  ]
}
```

kevin: agree. two small asks before merging: update the OpenAPI `components.schemas.EmbeddingsRequest` example to an array as well, and update the JS snippet generator to emit arrays not strings. there's a legacy template that formats `input` as a string if it's length 1. change to always render as array.

docs-bot: linting failed on PR: openapi example mismatch. Details: components.schemas.EmbeddingsRequest.example.input expected array, found string. CI log: https://ci.redwood-inference/1256/logs/234 :x:

marta: sorry, missed that in the MR. i'm updating the OpenAPI YAML now and will push. also adding a short migration blurb under /docs/migration/embedding-array.md explaining SDKs will auto-wrap single strings and recommending explicit arrays for high-throughput indexing jobs.

kevin: thanks. please also add a unit test to the docs build that asserts the generated page contains `"input": ["single string"]` so we don't regress back to string examples. i'll help wire that into the docs-test suite.

marta: test added and pushed. re-running CI.

docs-bot: CI passed on branch fix/docs-embed-request-example (build 482) :white_check_mark: https://ci.redwood-inference/1256/builds/482

oliver: merged. small follow-up requested: docs team to sync with SDKs to ensure Python/Go examples both show array usage. i've filed a tiny follow-up ticket for SDK snippets: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/900

sam: one more note from support: include a tiny Python example showing how to convert old single-string payloads to arrays for bulk indexing, e.g. `if isinstance(input, str): input = [input]`. i'll add that to the migration note.

marta: added the Python snippet and a Go example using a helper `wrapIfSingle` in the migration doc. closing thread. thanks everyone :tada:
